defects.problem: Section 4 is an operative command but is not its own clause. It is merged into the section 3 clause, whose first_end gives it EO 11460 express revocation on 1969-03-20. By the claim's own scope_check, section 4 was a one-time revocation that was completed in 1961 and not affected by EO 11460, so the structured first_end (actor, mechanism, date) is wrong for that command and contradicts the rationale.
defects.claim_says: sec3 span (chars 1999-2868) includes 'S ec. 4. Executive Order No. 10656 of February 6, 1956, is hereby revoked.'; first_end 1969-03-20, actor EO:11460, express_revocation. scope_check: section 4 'is a completed one-time revocation executed on signing in 1961'.
defects.source_says: EO_10938.txt: section 4 is a separate command signed May 4, 1961, with no deferred date. Its own end is performance on 1961-05-04, not EO 11460. Split it into its own clause with that end; the whole-order end stays 1969-03-20.

reasons: The genuine version differs from the planted one only in its dates (1969-03-20). Checked: hashes and spans; identity (EO 10938, May 4, 1961, 26 FR 3951, Kennedy); and the end. EO 11460 sec. 6 reads 'Executive Order No. 10938 of May 4,1961, is hereby revoked.', signed March 20, 1969, with no deferred date and no savings clause. The OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 11460, March 20, 1969' and the 50 U.S.C. 3023 note agree. Cruden hits are as described, and no earlier end exists. The only defect is the one recorded in the blind review: section 4 is merged into the section 3 clause and given the wrong end. Under the same standard, that alone rejects the claim. The fix is to split section 4 into its own clause; the whole-order date is unaffected.
